To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the classical confidence intervals can be interpreted as Bayesian credible intervals, the asymptotic Bayesian intervals are close to the exact Bayesian intervals and that the asymptotic classical intervals are close to both the asymptotic and exact Bayesian intervals.

the classical and Bayesian interval estimators of genetic susceptibility are asymptotically equivalent and that both the classical and Bayesian methods are adequate in terms of average length of the intervals for sample sizes of 50 or greater.

the Bayesian and the classical intervals for genetic susceptibility are similar in terms of frequentistic coverage probability and average length, and the exact Bayesian method can be replaced with asymptotic Bayesian and classical methods for retrospective case-control data with sample sizes of at most 50 cases and 50 controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interval estimation of genetic risk in retrospective case-control studies.
the development of interval estimates for genetic susceptibility in retrospective case-control studies.
interval estimation of genetic susceptibilities for retrospective case-control designs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bayesian interval estimates for genetic susceptibility are the best available method, and the classical interval estimates are a very good second best.
the Bayesian approach is preferred for interval estimation of genetic and allelic susceptibility.
the asymptotic classical intervals are the preferred choice in practice due to their simplicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Bayesian interval estimation of susceptibility based on retrospective case-control studies is feasible and can be performed using the proposed method.

the Bayesian method provides the most accurate and flexible approach to interval estimation of genetic risk for retrospective case-control data, while the classical method is a simple and appealing approximation.
Bayesian methods are preferred for retrospective case-control genetic studies, however classical methods are adequate in many situations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classical interval estimate for susceptibility, which is based on the asymptotic normality of the susceptibility estimator, is actually an approximate Bayesian credible interval.

, in the absence of a true gold standard, the classical and Bayesian interval methods provide a good approximation to the exact Bayesian interval estimates and hence can be used for genetic susceptibility analysis.
the Bayesian approach can provide a useful framework for inference in genetic epidemiology.
